draft.title: Food chains and food webs
card: Producer
an organism that makes its own food using sunlight, such as grass or algae.
Consumer
an organism that gets energy by eating other organisms, such as a kangaroo eating grass or a eagle eating a rabbit.
Decomposer
an organism that breaks down dead plants and animals, such as fungi and some bacteria.

A food chain shows one path of food through an ecosystem, with arrows pointing from the food to the eater. A food web links many food chains, because most organisms eat and are eaten by more than one kind.
draft.remember: Producers make food, consumers eat it, decomposers break down the dead. A web joins many chains.

a.q: In a bushland ecosystem, mushrooms grow on a fallen log and break it down. What is the role of the mushrooms?
opts: Decomposers
Producers
Consumers
Food chains
a.why: The mushrooms are fungi that break down dead plant matter, so they are decomposers. They are not producers, because they do not make food from sunlight.
a.clue: What are the mushrooms doing to the dead log?

b.q: In a Victorian wetland, algae are eaten by tadpoles. Tadpoles are eaten by fish, and algae are also eaten by water snails, which the fish eat too. Why is this a food web and not a single food chain?
opts: Several food chains are linked in one ecosystem
It has more than one producer in it
The arrows point from the eater to the food
Decomposers are shown at the end of each path
b.why: The tadpole path and the snail path both start with algae and end with fish, so the chains link together into a web. Having one producer does not make it a chain, and a single chain has no branches.
b.clue: Count the different paths that food can take.

b.best: Several food chains are linked in one ecosystem
